title: Strategy 1: The Global Reference (“The Bible”)
use_cases: Use when content consistency needs to be maintained across long-form generation
Implement when mapping modern real-world terms to fictional or thematic equivalents
Configure when character names and locations must remain immutable across multiple scenes
Apply when combating AI output drift in high-volume creative workflows
content:
- The Fix: We create a rigid JSON object called the Bible during Phase 2, and we pass it to every single scene generation call.
- The Problem: Drift. Over 120 pages, “John” becomes “Jon,” “Office” becomes “Headquarters,” and the tone slowly reverts to the original.

How it works: This isn’t a suggestion box; it’s a hard lock. The Bible contains explicit maps:

- The Result: By forcing the model to reference this “Source of Truth” every time it picks up the pen, we ensure that the fundamental facts of the universe never change.
- Prop Map: “iPhone” is now “Scroll”.
- Location Map: “OFFICE” is now “THRONE ROOM”.
- Character Profiles: “John” is now “ZEUS” (and he must stay “ZEUS” in Scene 50).
